heading_path: Required and optional relation fields in one-to-many relations
hits.tldr: One-to-many relations have a list field and an annotated field with scalar; both annotated sides must match in optionality.
One-to-many self-relations allow users to have optional teachers and zero or more students using Prisma schema.
One-to-many self-relations let a User model reference itself as both teacher and student.
Self-relations in SQL Server and MongoDB require explicit onDelete and onUpdate referential actions set to NoAction.

heading_path: Special rules for SQL Server and MongoDB
hits.tldr: Self-relations in SQL Server and MongoDB must explicitly set onDelete and onUpdate to NoAction to avoid cycles.

structuredContent.text:
## One-to-many self relations

```prisma
model User {
  id        Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
  name      String?
  teacherId Int?
  teacher   User?   @relation("TeacherStudents", fields: [teacherId], references: [id])
  students  User[]  @relation("TeacherStudents")
}
```

This expresses:

- A user has zero or one teacher
- A user can have zero or more students

No `@unique` constraint on `teacherId` - multiple students can share the same teacher.

content.text:
Your model needs two named, opposite relation fields — Prisma can't infer the back-relation on a self-referencing table automatically.

```prisma
model ProductCategory {
  id               Int               @id @default(autoincrement())
  name             String
  parentCategoryId Int?
  parentCategory   ProductCategory?  @relation("CategoryHierarchy", fields: [parentCategoryId], references: [id])
  subCategories    ProductCategory[] @relation("CategoryHierarchy")
  @@map("productCategories")
}
```

This gives one parent + many children per node, and since there's no depth limit on `parentCategoryId`, it naturally supports infinite nesting.

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/self-relations.mdx` — "One-to-many self relations" (lines 39–56).
